To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SARS CoV2 N protein forms liquid droplets with RNA and that N protein partitions into liquid droplets formed by human hnRNPs.

the intrinsically dis ordered N terminal IDR and the folded C terminal domain of the SARS CoV2 nucleocapsids protein are sufficient to phase separate with RNA, and that N protein phase separates with human hnRNPA2 and FUS, and with their LCs.

N condenses with RNA in a liquid liquid phase separation reaction that requires two disordered regions and the oligomerization domain and that N can be recruited in vitro to liquid liquid phase separated complexes of human RNA binding hnRNPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanisms by which the nucleocapsid proteins of coronaviruses and other viruses interact with their RNA genomes and with host proteins to form viral factories, the dynamic compartments in which viruses are assembled.
the role of LLPS in the formation of stress granules and other membraneless organelles and in viral replication.
the role of RNA in the assembly of viral particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N protein of SARS CoV2 can form liquid liquid phase separated droplets with RNA and with the low complexity domains of human hnRNP proteins, which are involved in SG assembly and function.
the SARS CoV2 nucleocapside protein is a multifunctional intrinsically disorded protein (IDP) with the capacity for liquid liquid phase separation with viral RNA and human stress granule proteins.
the N protein of SARS CoV-2 is a phase separating protein that can phase separate with RNA, with human hnRNPA2 and with human hnRNP TDP 43.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
N protein is a promiscuous phase separating protein that can be recruited into phase separated complexes with human RNA binding proteins.
N protein phase separates with genomic RNA and that N protein is recruited to phase separated forms of host proteins associated with SGs.

the N protein of SARS CoV2 can phase separate with RNA, and can be recruited to the phase separated forms of hnRNPs and their LC domains, which is likely a key mechanism for the role in viral genome packing and for co opting of host proteins for viral replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SARS CoV2 N protein can LLPS with both viral RNA and with human stress granule components, suggesting that the virus can hijack host stress granules to facilitate viral replication and spread.
the N protein from SARS CoV2 can phase separate with RNA in vitro and can also be recruited into the phase separated forms of the human hnRNPs TDP 43, hnRNPA1 and FUS.
N is an RNA binding protein with a multivalent RNA binding interface and that N protein phase separates with both viral RNA and host proteins involved in SG formation.
